title: Fallback Grid: orchestrated routing and rollback for heterogeneous canary / A-B / shadow rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As customers adopt model variants across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments we need a single, predictable control plane to route traffic during rollouts (shadow, canary, A/B) while ensuring graceful degradation across regions and capacity tiers. Existing routing is ad-hoc: region failover is manual, compatibility checks are limited, and automatic rollback only inspects error-rate spikes without considering degraded semantics (latency regressions, hallucination signals, token-cost anomalies).

Proposal: Implement a Fallback Grid service and control-plane primitives that combine: (1) a per-variant compatibility score (model->input schema + tokenizer + response format), (2) runtime health signals (latency P95, token cost delta, error-rate, semantic regression score), (3) region capacity tiers and proximity policies, and (4) configurable rollback policies for canary/A-B/shadow that operate across those dimensions.

Key components:
- Compatibility Scorer: offline preflight checks + lightweight runtime probes to detect schema or KV-cache incompatibilities. Outputs a discrete compatibility band (compatible | partial | incompatible) used during routing decisions.
- Health Aggregator: ingests Console metrics (latency, errors, token cost) and user-defined evaluation probes (prompt-set regressions). Emits health_tier (green|yellow|red) and trend signals.
- Fallback Grid Router: policy engine that maps traffic slices to variant endpoints with fallback waterfalls. Policies express priorities by region, customer tier (hosted/standard/dedicated), and capacity tier (reserve/spot/burst). Supports weighted A/B, shadow mirroring, and progressive canaries.
- Auto-Rollback Evaluator: rule DSL combining immediate SLO breaches (latency > threshold, error-rate > X) with slower semantic regressions (label drift on eval set). Supports hysteresis, rollback backoff, and safe-roll-forward paths (route to previous compatible variant or degrade to smaller-capacity variant in same region).
- Console integration: rollout UI shows Fallback Grid projection (expected routes), active fallbacks, and safety triggers; allows manual override and forced rollbacks.

Acceptence criteria (high level):
- New rollout policy can express region-aware failover + capacity-tier preference in YAML/Console UI.
- For a staged canary (1% -> 5% -> 20%), grid triggers automatic rollback within the configured windows on either acute SLO breaches or sustained semantic regression with documented hysteresis.
- Shadow traffic can be mirrored with zero customer impact and visibility into compatibility scorer mismatches.
- Integration tests that simulate multi-region partial-capacity loss and verify traffic shifts as policy dictates.

Why this differs from existing work: Prior tickets focus on canary mechanics, shadowing, and basic tiered fallbacks. This ticket consolidates those capabilities into a policy-first Grid abstraction that reasons about compatibility bands, semantic regression signals, and capacity tiers simultaneously. It emphasizes conservative default behaviors for Dedicated/Private customers and deterministic observability for operators.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Martinez: Created initial proposal. Collected background: existing canary and fallback tickets, and Console rollout UI mockups. Added acceptance criteria and rough component split.

2026-02-24 - Ravi Desai: Engineering review kickoff. Raised question about interaction with KV-cache warming for model variants; plan to add lightweight probe step in the Compatibility Scorer to prime caches on first mirror requests.

2026-03-02 - PM feedback (Lina Kurian): Asked for explicit behavior for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity — defaults should prefer same-region failover to avoid cross-tenant performance impacts. Added to design notes.

2026-03-04 - Design review (Mira Chen): Console mockups reviewed; suggested a stacked timeline view showing expected vs actual traffic allocations during rollout and a color-coded grid for compatibility bands. Linked design spec: https://drive.google.com/designs/redwood/fallback-grid-spec

2026-03-06 - Engineering note (Ravi): Spike completed for Compatibility Scorer. Prototype tests show we can detect tokenizer mismatches by sending a 50-sample probe set and verifying tokenization length variance. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1879

2026-03-08 - Reliability tests scheduled: synthetic multi-region outage planned to validate tiered failover logic (reserve->burst->cross-region). Test plan in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Fallback+Grid+Test+Plan

2026-03-10 - Ava: Decision log: default Grid policy for Hosted is conservative (prefer compatible variant in same region, then compatible variant cross-region, then previous stable variant). For Dedicated customers with pinned hardware, default is local rollback to previous variant and alert. Added requirement to surface rollback rationale in the Console event timeline.

2026-03-10 - Action items: (1) Implement Health Aggregator ingestion and smoothing (owner: Ravi, estimate 5), (2) Build router policy DSL and evaluation engine (owner: Samir Patel, estimate 8), (3) Console visualization (owner: Mira Chen, estimate 5).
